title: Protocol for fine casting, imaging, and analysis of murine vascular networks with VALID
protocol: Warm 0.01 M PBS to 40°C using a water bath.
Turn on the pump and drain the air with warm PBS.
Ensure that the pump pipe used for perfusion is filled with warm PBS.
Deeply anesthetize mice with a mixture of ketamine/xylazine (100/20 mg/kg) via intraperitoneal injection.
Transcardially perfuse mice with 0.01 M PBS to wash out blood.
Insert perfusion needles into the right ventricle and cut the left atrial appendage.
Turn off the perfusion pump and change PBS to prepared lipophilic dye solutions.
Perfuse 10–15 mL of dye solution into the mouse body under warm conditions.
After sufficient cooling, collect mouse organs and tissues carefully.
Place harvested mouse tissues/organs into a 50 mL tube containing 4% PFA.
Ensure the volume ratio of tissue to 4% PFA solution is greater than 1:10.
Store the tube in a 4°C refrigerator overnight for post-fixation.
Wash the fixed samples with 0.01 M PBS with gentle shaking, refreshing the PBS every 1 hour for at least three times.
Add agarose powder in pure water at a concentration of 4% and heat until fully dissolved.
Cool the agarose solution and immerse the desired samples into the solution until solidification occurs.
Slice the embedded samples into tissue sections of desired thickness using a commercial vibratome.
Fully immerse the thin tissue sections in blocking solution for 3–6 hours with gentle shaking at 37°C.
Transfer the tissue sections into primary antibody solution (1:500 diluted in antibody diluent buffer) for 0.5–1 day with gentle shaking at 37°C, ensuring full immersion of samples.
Wash the samples with PBST solution for at least 6 times (20 min per time) to remove residual primary antibodies.
Transfer the tissue sections into the secondary antibody solution (1:500 diluted in antibody diluent buffer) for 0.5–1 d with gentle shaking.
Ensure that the samples are fully immersed during incubation.
Wash the samples with PBST solution for 6 times (20 min per time) to remove residual primary antibodies.
Treat the samples with a sequence of methanol solutions: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%, 80%, 60%, 40% and 20%, 1 h for each step with gentle shaking.
Wash the samples with PBST for 1 h after methanol treatment.
Incubate the pre-treated samples in permeabilization solution at 37°C overnight.
Transfer the samples to blocking solution at 37°C for 1 d.
Wash the samples by PTwH (PBS + Triton X-100 + Tween 20 + HEPES) overnight.
Refresh the PTwH solutions for at least 6 times during washing.
Incubate the treated samples in primary antibody dilution at 37°C with gentle shaking for 2–3 d.
Wash the samples with PTwH for 1 d.
Refresh the PTwH solutions for at least 6 times during washing.
Incubate the samples in the secondary antibody dilution at 37°C with gentle shaking for 2–3 days.
Wash the tissues in PTwH for 1 day.
Refresh the PTwH solutions for at least 6 times.
Store the immunolabeled tissues in PBST/PTWH at this time if needed, for up to one week before clearing and imaging.
Store the immunolabeled samples at 4°C until use.
Prepare gradient methanol solutions at concentrations of 50%, 70%, 80%, 100%, and 100% using distilled water.
Prepare gradient ethanol solutions at concentrations of 50%, 70%, 80%, 100%, and 100% using distilled water.
Prepare gradient tetrahydrofuran (THF) solutions at concentrations of 50%, 70%, 80%, 100%, and 100% using distilled water.
Prepare gradient tert-butanol (TB) solutions at concentrations of 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 100%, and 100% using distilled water.
Dehydrate the prepared samples using THF solutions with concentration gradients of 50%, 70%, 80%, 100%, and 100% for 4 hours (tissue slices) or 12 hours (whole organs).
Transfer the dehydrated samples to pure dibenzyl ether (DBE) for refractive index matching until fully transparent.
Decalcify hard bones in 20% EDTA solution for 1–2 days.
Process decalcified bones with tissue clearing procedure.
Bleach samples in 1%-2% H2O2 for 30 minutes if autofluorescence is strong.
Prepare MACS-R0 by mixing 20 vol% MXDA and 15% (w/v) sorbitol with distilled water.
Prepare MACS-R1 by mixing 40 vol% MXDA and 30% (w/v) sorbitol in 1 × PBS.
Prepare MACS-R2 by mixing 40 vol% MXDA and 50% (w/v) sorbitol in distilled water.
Heat solution with a water bath to promote dissolution of sorbitol.
Incubate samples in 20–30 mL MACS-R0, MACS-R1, and MACS-R2 solutions in 50 mL conical tubes with gentle shaking at room temperature.
Use a laser-scanning confocal microscope (LSM710, Zeiss, Germany) for imaging tissue slices.
Image the cleared samples (e.g., brain, spinal cord, kidney, liver, etc.) with a light sheet microscope (LiTone XL, Light Innovation Technology, China).

Convert acquired imaging data files (.tif, .czi) to Imaris™ file (.ims) format by dragging and dropping the files into ‘Imaris™ File Converter’ or directly import the .tif files into Imaris and save as .ims file.
Open the vascular data files in 3D view within Imaris.
Set the image properties based on the parameters of imported image data (e.g., resolution for X, Y, Z axis).
Rotate the 3D image in the navigate function.
Obtain the snapshot image by clicking the ‘snapshot’ button at desired resolution.
Add a ‘filament’ to the current opened dataset.
Choose the “Threshold (loops)” algorithm in filaments module to trace and quantify blood vessels.
Manually adjust the threshold for extracting vascular information to ensure complete recognition of all blood vessels.
Reconstruct the vascular network.
Obtain local vessel density using the “statistics-selection” in filaments module.
Obtain average radius using the “statistics-selection” in filaments module.
Obtain vessel segment length using the “statistics-selection” in filaments module.
Export desired datasets as excel files.
